cards.name: Colored Pencil
cards.summary: Redraws the image as coloured-pencil hatching on plain paper: edges and textured areas keep rough, cross-hatched strokes in the image's own colours, while smooth areas drop out to a flat paper tone taken from the Background colour swatch and set lighter or darker by Paper Brightness.
use_for: hand-drawn / sketchbook treatment of a product or portrait photo for a poster or zine
turning a busy photo background into a light pencil texture behind headline type
children's-book or school-themed social posts
avoid: soft or low-contrast photos (like a video still): smooth areas vanish into flat paper and little is left to hatch; sharpen or raise contrast first

a monochrome ink sketch: use Filter/Sketch/Graphic Pen instead (one-direction strokes in the Foreground colour on Background-colour paper)

params.name: Pencil Width
params.does: thickness of the pencil strokes in pixels

params.name: Stroke Pressure
params.does: how dark and dense the pencil marks are; 0 leaves almost only paper

params.name: Paper Brightness
params.does: tone of the paper (the Background swatch) that replaces smooth areas: low = dark paper, high = near the swatch colour

pairs_with: set the Background swatch to a cream / parchment colour first to tint the paper

Filter/Convert for Smart Filters so it stays editable

cards.name: Cutout
cards.summary: Rebuilds the image from a few flat colour levels with simplified, smoothed outlines, as if made from roughly cut pieces of coloured paper; high-contrast subjects turn almost into silhouettes and fine detail merges away.
use_for: flat cut-paper / vector-like poster backgrounds from a photo
silhouette-style figures for an event flyer
simplifying a busy photo so overlaid type reads
avoid: faces that must stay recognisable: at low levels and high Edge Simplicity they collapse into blobs; keep Edge Fidelity 3 and 6-8 levels, or use Image/Adjustments/Posterize which keeps the outlines
real vector output: the result is still pixels; use Illustrator Image Trace for paths
text inside the photo: it is merged into the flat shapes and becomes illegible

cards.name: Dry Brush
cards.summary: Paints the image with a dry-brush technique (between oil and watercolour): colour ranges are simplified into patches of common colour and edges pick up dry, streaky brush marks, while overall tonality stays close to the original.
use_for: painterly poster or book-cover art from a photo
softening a photo background into a painted backdrop behind a cut-out subject
a quick illustrated look for event invitations
avoid: dark, contrasty fresco-like painting: that is Filter/Artistic/Fresco
small text or logos in the image: the brush simplification smears them
large print files (4000 px and up): every size slider is in pixels with a low maximum, so the strokes come out tiny and read as noise; work on a downsampled copy or use Filter > Stylize > Oil Paint

cards.name: Film Grain
cards.summary: Adds an even grain pattern to the shadows and midtones and a smoother, more saturated pattern to the lighter areas; raising Highlight Area also brightens and flattens the light tones. Used for a filmic texture and to hide banding in gradients or to unify images from different sources.
use_for: filmic / analog texture on a photo poster
breaking up banding in large gradients before print or export
making a composite of mismatched photos look like one shot
avoid: plain, colour-neutral grain only: Filter/Noise/Add Noise (Monochromatic) or the Grain adjustment layer (Layer/New Adjustment Layer/Grain) give cleaner grain (the adjustment layer also stays editable)
high Highlight Area on bright skin or white type: light tones wash out to flat white
Intensity: the harvest only shows its range (0-10); how it shapes the highlight effect was not verified

cards.name: Fresco
cards.summary: Repaints the image in a coarse fresco style with short, rounded, hastily applied dabs; shadows are darkened hard, so the result is high-contrast and heavy, with dark areas tending towards black.
use_for: dramatic painted poster or album art
a gritty mural / wall-painting look for a background
stylised editorial illustration from a photo
avoid: images that are already dark (dark suits, night shots): those areas go solid black and lose detail; brighten first or use Filter/Artistic/Dry Brush, which keeps the tonality
faces in close-up: the dark dabs read as blemishes
large print files (4000 px and up): every size slider is in pixels with a low maximum, so the strokes come out tiny and read as noise; work on a downsampled copy or use Filter > Stylize > Oil Paint

cards.name: Neon Glow
cards.summary: Colourises and softens the image into a near-monochrome tint and adds a glow of the chosen Color along its tones; the current Foreground / Background swatches also enter the mix, so the result changes with them (exact mix not verified here). It is a colour-wash glow over the whole image, not a neon-tube outline.
use_for: dreamy / night-time single-tint poster backgrounds

pushing a photo into a brand colour with a glow
avoid: a real neon-tube outline: use Filter/Stylize/Glowing Edges, or Layer/Layer Style/Outer Glow on a stroked shape or type layer
photos whose original colours must survive: they are replaced by the tint
unpredictable colour: reset the Foreground / Background swatches to default black / white before running so the result repeats
